newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin sacks Russian land forces chief - Interfax.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin sacks Russian land forces chief - Interfax.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin has sacked the commander of Russia's land forces for "actions incompatible with his post", Interfax news agency said on Monday.
The agency, quoting Russia's Defence Ministry, said Yeltsin had signed an order sacking General Vladimir Semyonov on Saturday. It did specify what Semyonov was being accused of.
"The commander has been sacked 'for actions which discredit honour and dignity of a serviceman and are incompatible with his post'," Interfax said.
The Kremlin press service could not immediately confirm the report.
Semyonov, 56, a career officer, commanded the land forces of the Soviet Union for a brief period in 1991, until the superpower collapsed in December of that year.
He was appointed chief of the Russian land forces in 1992. In June 1996, Yeltsin promoted him to the rank of the army general.
The wording of Yeltsin's decree appeared unusual for Russia, where most sackings of top officials are phrased vaguely, most often "due to a transfer to another job".
Defence Minister Igor Rodionov, appointed in July, is trying to install his authority in the top ranks.
The Russian military, humiliated by determined rebels in breakaway Chechnya, is now pulling out of the region in line with a Yeltsin decree.
Officers are crying out for extra funds, both to pay servicemen and to prevent the disintegration of the forces.
